item.title: Abuse of authority not tolerated: FCS
item.description: The Fiji Corrections Service (FCS) has launched an investigation into an alleged assault at the Lautoka Remand Centre, saying any abuse of authority by officers will not be tolerated. The investigation follows the circulation of a video on social media showing an incident involving a prison officer and an inmate.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Corrections Service (FCS) has launched an investigation into an alleged assault at the Lautoka Remand Centre, saying any abuse of authority by officers will not be tolerated.

The investigation follows the circulation of a video on social media showing an incident involving a prison officer and an inmate.

In a statement issued today, FCS confirmed it was aware of the incident and had commissioned an investigation to establish the facts surrounding the alleged assault and determine the appropriate course of action.

“The Fiji Corrections Service also confirms that assault by an officer against a prisoner or vice versa is not tolerated and anyone found to abuse his or her authority will face the full brunt of the law,” FCS said.

The Service said the investigation would determine the circumstances surrounding the incident and any further action required.

FCS assured members of the public that a comprehensive update would be provided once the investigation had been concluded.

item.title: CCTV footage triggers FCS probe into alleged prison assault
item.description: The Fiji Corrections Service (FCS) has launched an investigation into the assault of an inmate by a prison officer at the Lautoka Corrections facility after a CCTV video of the incident surfaced on social media. The video, dated June 14 this year, showed the officer dragging the inmate before repeatedly punching and kicking him.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Corrections Service (FCS) has launched an investigation into the assault of an inmate by a prison officer at the Lautoka Corrections facility after a CCTV video of the incident surfaced on social media.

The video, dated June 14 this year, showed the officer dragging the inmate before repeatedly punching and kicking him.

It is understood the incident occurred after the inmate allegedly swore at the officer.

The footage has prompted public concern over the conduct of prison officers and the treatment of inmates within the country’s correctional facilities.

When contacted, FCS confirmed it was investigating the matter and said a statement would be released soon.

item.title: UN warns of heat surge
item.description: PACIFIC island nations are on alert after the United Nations warned of unprecedented ocean warming expected to intensify this month. Rising temperatures threaten island communities, food security and fragile coastal ecosystems, with almost every land area on Earth forecast to experience above-normal temperatures.
item.content:encoded:
PACIFIC island nations are on alert after the United Nations warned of unprecedented ocean warming expected to intensify this month.

Rising temperatures threaten island communities, food security and fragile coastal ecosystems, with almost every land area on Earth forecast to experience above-normal temperatures.

In a global alert issued on Friday, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said sea-surface temperatures in key areas were expected to rise by three degrees Celsius.

“Two months ago, I warned that El Niño was arriving on our doorstep. Now it is inside the house and turning up the heat,” he said.

“We are in uncharted territory, and El Niño does not bring heat alone, it profoundly affects the world’s rainfall.”

Minister for Agriculture, Waterways and Sugar Tomasi Tunabuna said the Government had plans in place but urged communities to prepare for climate impacts.

“One of the programs that addresses this is nature-based solution seawalls, where rocks and soil are used to hold the structure. We are also working on drainage issues to avoid saltwater intrusion and channel water back to the ocean,” he said.

Mr Tunabuna said funding remained a challenge, but the Government was working with climate-focused donors and partners through the ridge-to-reef approach to strengthen community resilience.

“We do understand that we may be restricted in funding from the budget, which is why we reach out to donors,” he said.

Mr Guterres called for urgent global action through early warning systems, workplace heat standards, improved urban infrastructure and a phase-out of fossil fuels.

item.title: Character is your commander, school cadets told
item.description: NATABUA High School cadets were reminded that character was their commander during the school’s annual cadet corps passing-out parade in Lautoka yesterday. Chief guest and Tertiary Scholarships and Loans Service chief executive officer Dr Apisalome Movono urged cadets to embrace discipline, teamwork and leadership while making the right choices.
item.content:encoded:
NATABUA High School cadets were reminded that character was their commander during the school’s annual cadet corps passing-out parade in Lautoka yesterday.

Chief guest and Tertiary Scholarships and Loans Service chief executive officer Dr Apisalome Movono urged cadets to embrace discipline, teamwork and leadership while making the right choices.

“Cadet training is not just about matching and responding to the commands of your superiors; it is about building character,” he said.

“It teaches you, even us here, members of the audience, that discipline matters, teamwork is important, and it is especially important today because you, our young people, face many immense challenges.

“There will be times, ladies and gentlemen and cadets, when no teacher, parent or instructor is present — in those moments, your character is your commander.”

Cadets staged special formations on the parade ground, including a broken syringe and clenched fist to raise awareness about illicit drugs.

They formed “NAT 26” for the cadet corps and displayed the 2026 Commonwealth Games logo above “DI CEVA” in support of deputy head girl and national athlete Adi Ceva Lutumailagi, who is competing at the Games in Glasgow, Scotland.

item.title: Man in custody over boy’s death
item.description: A 29-YEAR-OLD man is in police custody following the death of an 11-year-old boy in Wailoku, Suva. Police said the boy was reported missing by his mother before his body was discovered near his home at around midday on Friday.
item.content:encoded:
A 29-YEAR-OLD man is in police custody following the death of an 11-year-old boy in Wailoku, Suva.

Police said the boy was reported missing by his mother before his body was discovered near his home at around midday on Friday.

The Fiji Times understands the boy was last seen on Wednesday evening while playing at a neighbour’s house and did not return home.

According to eyewitnesses, several children had been playing together on Wednesday afternoon while the adults were inside preparing for dinner.

When the children were called in for dinner at around 7pm, it was discovered the 11-year-old was missing.

Neighbours and family members searched for the boy throughout Wednesday night and continued the search on Thursday.

According to neighbours, the boy was last seen following another boy around the area.

His body was found on Friday morning behind an abandoned house some distance from his home.

Witnesses also alleged that the man now in police custody was seen fleeing the scene around the time the boy’s body was found.

The family has declined to comment as they mourn the loss of their child.

item.title: Water relief plan for Mali
item.description: A LONG-TERM solution to water shortages affecting two villages in Mali district in Macuata has been identified, with consultations underway with landowners before the project can proceed. While Vesi Village continues to have a reliable water source, acting commissioner Northern Apolosi Lewaqai said Ligaulevu and Nakawaga villages remained vulnerable during prolonged dry periods.
item.content:encoded:
A LONG-TERM solution to water shortages affecting two villages in Mali district in Macuata has been identified, with consultations underway with landowners before the project can proceed.

While Vesi Village continues to have a reliable water source, acting commissioner Northern Apolosi Lewaqai said Ligaulevu and Nakawaga villages remained vulnerable during prolonged dry periods.

“The Vesi Village water source remains relatively reliable, with adequate water catchment capacity to meet the community’s needs throughout most of the year,” he said.

Mr Lewaqai said Ligaulevu and Nakawaga depended mainly on groundwater boreholes and rainwater harvesting systems.

“During prolonged dry periods and drought conditions, water shortages are experienced in both villages.

“To ensure continued access to safe water, the (Waterways) ministry supports these communities by providing fuel assistance for the transportation of water from the mainland, specifically from Mali and Vorovoro.”

He said the Government had strengthened water security by installing water storage tanks in the three villages.

“As a long-term and sustainable solution, a potential water source has been identified at Matalabasa.”

He said the Mali district representative and village elders had started consultations with relevant landowners to obtain consent.

Upon securing the landowner agreements, he said the Water Authority of Fiji would be engaged to undertake assessments, scoping and engineering design works for the proposed water supply scheme.

item.title: Communities urged to lead crime fight
item.description: COMMUNITIES have been urged to take a leading role in the fight against crime, with Tui Macuata Ratu Wiliame Katonivere saying the responsibility does not rest solely with the police and the Government. Speaking during the Northern Crime Prevention Carnival in Labasa, Ratu Wiliame said crime affected families, businesses and the future of young people, making community participation essential.
item.content:encoded:
COMMUNITIES have been urged to take a leading role in the fight against crime, with Tui Macuata Ratu Wiliame Katonivere saying the responsibility does not rest solely with the police and the Government.

Speaking during the Northern Crime Prevention Carnival in Labasa, Ratu Wiliame said crime affected families, businesses and the future of young people, making community participation essential.

“We, the communities, are the first line of defence,” he said.

“When community members remain alert, report suspicious activities, support crime prevention programs and work closely with the police, we create safer neighbourhoods for everyone and secure a better future.”

He said criminals thrived in communities that remained silent but struggled where people stood together with courage and unity.

He acknowledged the efforts of community leaders, village elders, faith-based organisations, youth groups and the Fiji Police Force in raising awareness and encouraging vigilance.

“Their dedication has empowered many communities to recognise illegal activities and take responsible action before crime takes root,” he said.

He also called on parents, schools and churches to play a stronger role in guiding young people. He said parents needed to be actively involved in their children’s lives, while schools and churches should continue teaching positive values.

He urged communities to work hand in hand with law enforcement agencies to build safer neighbourhoods and leave a secure future for generations to come.

item.title: Seawall project awaits materials
item.description: CONSTRUCTION of nature-based seawalls for three villages on Mali Island will begin once shipping arrangements are confirmed. Acting Commissioner Northern Apolosi Lewaqai said the Ministry of Waterways had already secured materials needed for the project.
item.content:encoded:
CONSTRUCTION of nature-based seawalls for three villages on Mali Island will begin once shipping arrangements are confirmed.

Acting Commissioner Northern Apolosi Lewaqai said the Ministry of Waterways had already secured materials needed for the project.

“Materials for the construction of the nature-based seawalls have already been procured through the ministry’s internal funding allocation,” he said.

Mr Lewaqai said the project was awaiting confirmation of shipping schedules and the availability of a barge to transport the materials to the island communities.

“The project is currently awaiting confirmation of shipping schedules and the availability of barge transportation to facilitate the delivery of materials to the island communities.”

He said work would begin once transport arrangements had been finalised.

“Once transportation logistics have been finalised, construction activities will commence,” he said.

He said the project formed part of the ministry’s commitment to protecting vulnerable coastal communities from climate change and natural hazards.

“This initiative forms part of the ministry’s broader commitment to strengthening the resilience of vulnerable coastal communities against the adverse effects of climate change and natural hazards.”
